newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall St slipstream pulls Euroshares higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall St slipstream pulls Euroshares higher.

text.p: European shares were wafted higher on Friday by the second 80 point rise on Wall St in a row, but the buying in Europe was not as enthusiastic as on Thursday.
"It looks like the U.S. bull market isn't over just yet," the head of trading at a large brokerage in London said.
Elsewhere, the dollar was steady but gold was in retreat on worries that central banks could be selling bullion.

By 1000 GMT, London's FTSE index of top shares had climbed 22.1 points, or 0.52 percent, to 4,250.5, while in Frankfurt the DAX index was up 15.65 points, or 0.52 percent, at 3,032.97. But France's CAC 40 index was up just 3.0 points, or 0.12 percent, at 2.506.06.
Wall Street's Dow Jones industrial average ended up 83.12 points at 6,823.86 overnight, extending Wednesday's gain of 85 points, which was its first gain after five days of losses.
Over the last two days the Dow has recouped two-thirds of what it lost during its five-day skid.
The U.S. market was relieved that Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan did not come out with any surprises in his congressional testimony about the economy.

In testimony before the Senate Finance Committee, the Fed chief gave little hint that the central bank was considering raising interest rates at the February 4 and 5 meeting of the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee.
Higher interest rates would sorely test the world's share markets, many of which are at or near record levels, by making returns on alternative investments and cash more attractive.
Dealers in London said provided the Dow remained steady, the FTSE was set to test its all-time highs of 4,273.4 set on January 23 over the next few sessions.
"There is still room for a setback on Wall Street but sentiment seems to favour a re-test of the highs," a head of sales and trading at a major investment bank in London said.

Germany's DAX index romped higher in early trade, nearing its all time high of 3041.55. Software firm SAP rose 10 percent after posting stronger-than expected 1996 earnings. Porsche also soared after first-half profits surged.
Earlier, the IBIS DAX electronic index set a record intraday high of 3,050.88 in pre-bourse trade.
In France, Europe's most bullish market on Thursday, shares were also higher. But traders warned the market may consolidate later in the day ahead of the expiry of the CAC futures.
"Things are moving too fast," one dealer said, adding market euphoria may be short-lived.
In currencies, the dollar was drifting against the mark and yen in morning Europe with the market awaiting the fourth-quarter U.S. gross domestic product data due to be released at 1330 GMT.
The pound was vulnerable after heavy selling against the dollar and yen spilled over into mark trade too. By 1040 GMT, the pound was just above $1.60 and at 2.6160 marks.

Analysts said the dollar's mood was still bullish amid the lull, although there seemed to be some hesitation about pushing it higher in the wake of recent dollar-dampening comments from German and Japanese officials.

"The market is revolving around the GDP figures now...it's going to provide the benchmark against which the dollar's move is likely to be assessed," said Stephen Hannah, director of research at IBJ International.
The dollar was at 1.6339 marks and 121.40 yen at 1040 GMT.

"The dollar's going to be firmish today, seeing that we're expecting a strong number for the GDP... I don't think anyone's looking for less than 3.5 percent (growth)," said Brian Hilliard, chief economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
A Reuters poll of economists showed U.S. GDP for the fourth quarter of 1996 was expected to show growth of 3.9 percent after a rise of 2.1 percent previously.
The price of gold crumbled after a fresh rash of sales overnight sparked heavy long liquidation, pushing it to new three-year lows. Platinum was also weak.
"Most of the sales we have seen have been long liquidations by traders who thought we'd seen the worst," said Jonathan Spall, head of precious metals for Deutsche Bank in Hong Kong.
Rumours of central bank gold sales continued to undermine the price and dealers in Asia said the price could head for $340 and even $320 an ounce.
CURRENCIES AT 1040 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6339 marks and 121.40 yen, compared with late Thursday's European levels of 1.6382 marks and 121.61 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1045 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was up 14.7 points at 4,243.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 3.48 points at 2,506.54.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 11.09 points at 3,028.41.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fell to $344.85 in early European trade after a drop in the United States and closing at $347.35 in Europe on Thursday.
